verdict.rationale: Notion documents two credential types with meaningful scoping: internal integrations use a static token scoped to a single workspace, and public/OAuth integrations let developers choose an installation scope at creation time — both directly relevant to issuing least-privilege credentials for an agent. However, the evidence doesn't detail fine-grained permission scopes (e.g., read-only vs. write, per-capability restrictions) or agent-specific credential issuance workflows. Missing for 10: documented granular capability-level scopes (read/insert/update/no-content), explicit agent-oriented credential provisioning guidance, and independent/hands-on verification of scope enforcement.
